title: Celia Cruz's birth chart
metaDescription: Celia Cruz's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.8° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Pluto sit 0.2° from an exact square — near enough that the tradition reads drive and depth as a single working part. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Libra, but precisely: 27.8°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Mercury in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 7.3° Scorpio, Venus was at 11.7° Sagittarius, Mars was at 14.9° Libra. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Saturn to Pluto, a trine with 0.0° of slack. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, Mars square Pluto at 0.2°, and Mars square Jupiter at 0.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Pluto while both square Mars. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Libra at 27.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Libra at 14.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Capricorn at 15.4° is in fall. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 4, fire 3, air 2, earth 1 across the elements, and cardinal 4, mutable 3, fixed 3 across the modalities. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 17.8°.
